summary: Reel hooks lose 77% viewers in first 3 seconds; chatbot posts earn 1/5 of lead_gen per reach. Instagram bio violates brand rules (niche, region, timeframe, permanent free offer).
guidance:
- Hook style: try **contrast** or **comparison** (avoid question — Instagram data shows 21% of comparison performance).
- Angle: use **mistake** framing (1.33x in learning loop) — e.g., "The mistake of assuming a chatbot replaces human touch."
- Avoid repeating "same 5 questions" or "busy with walk-in" — used in last two chatbot posts.
- Image style: **desk-glow** or **glass-ui** (top performers).
- Posts must read as a developer showing real work, never an ad. No demos, no niche targeting, no guaranteed outcomes.

instructions.research: Find 2-3 common chatbot misconceptions Indian small businesses have (cost, complexity, language) — cite generic sources, no client specifics.
instructions.analysis: Compare last 3 chatbot posts' hooks/angles; note which got any engagement (even low) to avoid repetition.
instructions.writer: Write a contrast/comparison post: mistake angle, 2-3 example business types max, soft wording ("can reduce", "helps"), offer pay-after-approval + DM for honest fit check. No demo claims.
instructions.image: Create a desk-glow or glass-ui static image: split screen showing "Before bot: missed WhatsApp at 10 PM" vs "After bot: auto-reply + lead captured" — no brand logos, generic UI.
instructions.video: Skip reel today; static image performs better for chatbot topic. If video later, hook in first 1s: "Most bots fail because..." (contrast).

manual_tips: Update Instagram bio to: "Websites, AI chatbots, animated ads & lead gen for small businesses across India. Pay after approval. DM for honest advice."
Comment on 5 posts by Indian freelancers/agencies discussing client acquisition — add value, no self-promo.
Reply to any story/reel about small business operations (WhatsApp overload, after-hours queries) with a genuine observation, no pitch.
